spec.title: vscode PROP-010: Licensing - where this family states a licence

status.comment: the type's answer to the twelfth area of the contract (2026-11-01, campaign licensing-area); the profile, the header layout, the writing of the surfaces, the annotation of own files and the checks stay in the engine (modules/codkit/PROP-019)

p.VSCODE-LICENSING-AREA: The type declares the capability `licensing` and answers the area (`spec://codkit/modules/codkit/PROP-016#TYPE-AREA-LICENSING`): `headerStyle: block` - own files carry the ruled comment the sources of this distribution carry, so own code reads as one system with the code beside it (`MI-SAME-SHAPE-AS-UPSTREAMS-PARALLEL-SYSTEM`); `licenceFileDirectory: ''` (the root); `componentLicenceDirectory: 'licenses'`; `subsystem: 'product'`; the fields, the upstream licence file, the rendering and the guard stated below. A type writes nothing: the engine lays headers out from the profile, writes the overlays, the add-file patches, the rendering and the guard, and checks them back.

p.VSCODE-LICENCE-FIELDS: Five fields of two overlay targets declare the licence of the product. In `product.json`: `licenseName` (`expression`; the upstream carries the identifier of its own licence there), `licenseFileName` (`file-name`; the build of this distribution copies the file this key names from the root into the application beside `ThirdPartyNotices.txt` and `licenses/**`, which is why the key and not a path of the build is the surface), `licenseUrl` and `serverLicenseUrl` (`url`; the upstream points them at its repository, and a product without a published URL removes them, which also hides the "view licence" entry of the help menu). In `package.json`: the key `license` (`expression`), which the overlay target admits as a guarded scalar replacement beside the additions under `scripts` since 2026-11-01 (`spec://codkit/modules/vscode/PROP-003#VSCODE-OVERLAY-TARGETS`).

files.title: 2. The licence file, the component licences and the installer

p.VSCODE-LICENCE-FILE-AT-ROOT: The product's licence file lives at the tree root under the name the product chose (`product.licenseFile` of its declaration, `LICENSE.md` by default): `build/gulpfile.vscode.ts` copies `product.licenseFileName` from the root into the application, so the name in the manifest and the file at the root are one surface, written together by `gen licensing`. The upstream's `LICENSE.txt` stays where it is: it carries the upstream's own terms, it is never edited, and it stops being the product's licence only because the manifest no longer names it.

p.VSCODE-COMPONENT-LICENCES: `licenses/` is the component directory: the build copies `licenses/**` into the application, so `licenses/LICENSE-code-oss.txt` (the upstream's `LICENSE.txt` byte for byte at the pin; the component is named after the upstream's own name for its open build) and `licenses/LICENSE-codkit.txt` (the tool's own licence text, present because the runtime library is delivered into `src/vs/<own>/codkit/**` and compiled into the product) travel with every distributable. `ThirdPartyNotices.txt` is not a surface of this area: it is the upstream's notices file for the upstream's dependencies and stays untouched.

p.VSCODE-INSTALLER-RTF: The Windows installer of this distribution (`build/win32/code.iss`) shows `LICENSE.rtf` from the root when the file exists and `LICENSE.txt` otherwise, and reads only text or RTF. The type therefore asks for one rendering, `LICENSE.rtf` at the root in the format `rtf`, which the engine writes from the canonical text, so the installer shows the product's terms without a change to the installer script. A rendering per installer language (`licenses/LICENSE-<language>.rtf`, which the script also looks for) is an owner's decision recorded in the campaign plan (RP-1).

p.VSCODE-LICENCE-GUARD: The guard is written at `delta/own/test/node/licence.leftovers.test.ts` - the own tests of this family live under `<ownRoot>/test/<layer>/` and run under the distribution's Mocha-style runner - with the words `suite` and `test`; it reads the tree from the directory the runner starts in, which is the tree root for the test scripts of this distribution, and names no path of the tool. Its preamble is one line: the directive that excuses the suite from the family's disposable-leak rule (`local/code-ensure-no-disposables-leak-in-test`) with its reason - the guard reads files and asserts and creates no disposable (2026-11-01: the first generated guard lit 162 warnings of the family's lint on the pilot, 161 of them the `curly` rule, which the template now satisfies by bracing every branch).
